cim: Tech experts say recent outages could be tied to artificial intelligence updates
cim_eredeti: Tech experts say recent outages could be tied to artificial intelligence updates
szoveg_eredeti:
A series of high-profile outages, including disruptions to Microsoft Outlook, airport ground stops, and Chase Bank systems, have been linked to proactive upgrades addressing flaws and vulnerabilities exposed by advanced AI tools.

Jon Salisbury, CEO and cofounder of Nexigen, a Newport-based cybersecurity company, explained that recent advancements in AI and cybersecurity tools have enabled organizations to identify and address previously undiscovered flaws.

"In April, different companies like Anthropic, OpenAI, and other leading security research groups that we interact with as well, basically provided advanced code analysis tools and then also cyber tools," Salisbury said.

He noted that many organizations are now racing to improve their systems simultaneously, which has contributed to the clustering of outages.

"Everyone's in a race to get into a better posture because we're now capable of a better posture that tools, and AI tools, helped us get better," Salisbury said.

Salisbury likened the situation to pothole maintenance on physical roads, explaining that while the upgrades are proactive, they can lead to temporary disruptions.

"We're making the roads better, this is actually proactive. And then on the way of being proactive, we're seeing some hiccups that occur. And when we see those hiccups, those are actually opportunities to improve further," Salisbury said.

While none of the outages have been linked to cyberattacks, experts suggest that some disruptions may be tied to the ongoing work to prevent such attacks.
